controls.label: Monochrome
controls.notes: JAXA’s mapped 548.9 nm reflectance from the 10 July 2018 BOX-A observations. The source grid is 0.2° per pixel and missing values are explicitly marked. This monochrome view uses the published corrected reflectance, with a display stretch; it does not reconstruct missing poles.

controls.label: Enhanced color
controls.notes: The mapping team’s published color composite assigns the p, v and ul filters to red, green and blue. It includes near-infrared light and is not natural color. Global brightness and contrast were matched across observations, so these mosaic values are unsuitable for quantitative photometry. Local residual shadows remain.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.notes: Color shows radius minus a 448 m reference sphere, including the body's broad irregular shape. This is not gravitational height or an image observation. Brightness adds cartographic relief from the full source model; Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting. Fine terrain is represented in the map while the displayed silhouette is simplified. Values follow the nearest corresponding point on the full source shape within the display mesh’s simplification allowance. This is radial height, not gravitational height; flat previews withhold overlapping radial surfaces.

controls.label: Equatorial close-up
controls.notes: Images taken by Hayabusa2 during MASCOT deployment show boulders across Ryugu’s equatorial strip. The original sampling is about 28 cm per pixel; the display is coarser. Brightness includes the illumination when the photographs were taken. The grid marks gaps and the unobserved poles.

controls.label: Thermal inertia
controls.notes: False colors show how slowly the surface heats and cools, inferred from a thermal model fitted to Hayabusa2 observations. Higher values mean slower temperature changes. This is a thermal property, not a temperature map. The underlying observations sampled roughly 4.5 m per pixel; the finer map grid adds no measured detail. The grid marks missing values.

controls.label: Spectral slope
controls.notes: False colors show the change in reflectance from blue to near-infrared light (b–x bands). Positive values mean a redder spectrum; negative values mean bluer. This does not measure terrain slope or identify minerals. The source’s saturated ±1 endpoints are withheld, and the grid marks those pixels. Polar mapping artifacts remain.
